answer_text:
We need to evaluate

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n\left[\left(n^5+5n^4\right)^{1/5}-\left(n^2+2n\right)^{1/2}\right].
\]

Factor out the dominant powers:

\[
\left(n^5+5n^4\right)^{1/5}
= n\left(1+\frac{5}{n}\right)^{1/5},
\]

and

\[
\left(n^2+2n\right)^{1/2}
= n\left(1+\frac{2}{n}\right)^{1/2}.
\]

Use the binomial expansion \((1+x)^\alpha = 1+\alpha x+\frac{\alpha(\alpha-1)}{2}x^2+O(x^3)\).

For the first term, with \(\alpha=\frac15\) and \(x=\frac5n\),

\[
\left(1+\frac{5}{n}\right)^{1/5}
=1+\frac15\cdot\frac5n+\frac{\frac15\left(-\frac45\right)}{2}\left(\frac5n\right)^2+O\left(\frac1{n^3}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
\left(1+\frac{5}{n}\right)^{1/5}
=1+\frac1n-\frac{2}{n^2}+O\left(\frac1{n^3}\right).
\]

Multiplying by \(n\),

\[
\left(n^5+5n^4\right)^{1/5}
= n+1-\frac{2}{n}+O\left(\frac1{n^2}\right).
\]

For the second term, with \(\alpha=\frac12\) and \(x=\frac2n\),

\[
\left(1+\frac{2}{n}\right)^{1/2}
=1+\frac12\cdot\frac2n+\frac{\frac12\left(-\frac12\right)}{2}\left(\frac2n\right)^2+O\left(\frac1{n^3}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
\left(1+\frac{2}{n}\right)^{1/2}
=1+\frac1n-\frac{1}{2n^2}+O\left(\frac1{n^3}\right).
\]

Multiplying by \(n\),

\[
\left(n^2+2n\right)^{1/2}
= n+1-\frac{1}{2n}+O\left(\frac1{n^2}\right).
\]

Now subtract:

\[
\left(n^5+5n^4\right)^{1/5}-\left(n^2+2n\right)^{1/2}
=
\left(n+1-\frac{2}{n}\right)-\left(n+1-\frac{1}{2n}\right)+O\left(\frac1{n^2}\right).
\]

So

\[
\left(n^5+5n^4\right)^{1/5}-\left(n^2+2n\right)^{1/2}
=
-\frac{3}{2n}+O\left(\frac1{n^2}\right).
\]

Therefore,

\[
n\left[\left(n^5+5n^4\right)^{1/5}-\left(n^2+2n\right)^{1/2}\right]
=
n\left(-\frac{3}{2n}+O\left(\frac1{n^2}\right)\right)
=
-\frac32+O\left(\frac1n\right).
\]

Taking the limit as \(n\to\infty\),

\[
\boxed{-\frac32}
\]
